svg.title: MN 70 Kīṭāgiri Sutta — At Kīṭāgiri
svg.desc: Discourse illustration for MN 70: The discipline of eating only during the day, the discernment of feelings by spiritual consequence, who must act with diligence, the seven kinds of persons, the gradual twelve-step cascade to final knowledge, and the unyielding resolve of the faithful disciple.

g.text: At Kīṭāgiri · The Discipline of Meals, Discernment of Feeling & the Gradual Path
“Final knowledge is not attained from the very beginning — but through gradual training, practice, and progress.”
na ādikeneva aññārādhanaṁ vadāmi … anupubbasikkhā anupubbakiriyā anupubbapaṭipadā aññārādhanā hoti
THE DISCIPLINE OF MEALS & THE HEDONIC EXCUSE
Day eating brings five bodily benefits; comfort in negligence is mistaken for the goal
Physical restraint supports clarity and ease in meditation
sāyañceva … pāto ca divā ca vikāle
“We experience fewer illnesses and comfort eating
in evening, morning, and outside proper time.”
“Why abandon what is evident here and now (sandiṭṭhika)
to pursue what belongs to time (kālika)?”
They confuse hedonic ease with spiritual completion
Self-justification grounded in unexamined bodily comfort
Felt experience does not validate conduct: evaluate feelings solely by wholesome growth vs unwholesome growth
“Do I teach that whatever one feels, wholesome states grow?” — NO.
ñātaṁ diṭṭhaṁ viditaṁ sacchikataṁ phassitaṁ paññāya · known through wisdom
Judge by growth of wholesome states — never by momentary comfort
WHO MUST ACT WITH DILIGENCE? · APPAMĀDENA KARAṆĪYAṂ
“I do not say of all that they have work to do with diligence; nor do I say of all that they have no work to do”
No more work to be done with diligence:
• Completed what had to be done (katakaraṇīyā)
kataṁ tesaṁ appamādena · abhabbā te pamajjituṁ
Still have work to do with diligence:
Striving for unsurpassed security from bondage (yogakkhema)
Fruit of diligence: Awakening here and now
diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyyuṁ
THE SEVEN KINDS OF PERSONS · SATTA PUGGALĀ
Two have finished; five still train with diligence
• Touches formless with body kāyena phusitvā
• Taints ended by wisdom āsavā parikkhīṇā
• Taints ended by wisdom āsavā parikkhīṇā
Same three supports as the trainees above ↑ dwellings · good friends · balanced faculties
6–7 bear the five faculties in seed form
“Final knowledge is attained through gradual training, gradual practice, and gradual progress”
Touched with body · penetrated with wisdom · paññāya ativijjha passati
The conduct of a faithful disciple intent on deeply penetrating the Teacher’s Dhamma
“The Teacher knows, I do not know.”
satthā bhagavā, sāvakohamasmi; jānāti bhagavā, nāhaṁ jānāmi
Instruction becomes nourishing for growth ruḷhanīyaṁ ojavantaṁ
“Let skin, sinews, bones remain — flesh and blood dry up —
striving shall not slacken till the goal is won.”
kāmaṁ taco ca nhāru ca aṭṭhi ca avasissatu …
Two fruits: ① Final knowledge here and now diṭṭheva dhamme aññā
or ② Non-Returning if clinging remains sati upādisese anāgāmitā
